attrs.evidence: schema.mjs `ownSnapshot` (canonicalise once, re-parse into plain data), applied as an ingress wrapper to ALL FOUR protocols -- proof_check.mjs, domain_check.mjs, compose_check.mjs and nest_check.mjs -- with named `*-ingress-refused` codes rather than an escaping exception. nest_check.mjs additionally exposes `checkNestBytes`. Gate `gov-nest`, and grid probe `input-read-once`: a live getter is read EXACTLY ONCE by each checker, measured on P4 and P1 together, and a getter returning the hostile value AT INGRESS is refused so the single read is load-bearing rather than lucky.
attrs.statement: A VERIFIER COMPUTES A VERDICT FROM ONE IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT IT OWNS, TAKEN AT INGRESS. After ingress no semantic check, identity computation, policy decision, measurement or diagnostic may reread caller-owned state. A checker handed a live host-language OBJECT is handed something the caller can still change, and one getter is enough: measured against the shipped P4.1 pack on TWO protocols at once, `references.contract.address_is_a_warrant` returned false to the first read and true to every later one while checkNestBundle returned VERIFIED and the same object then serialised with address_is_a_warrant true; and `claim.scope.generalizes_beyond_domain` returned false for the three reads P1's checker makes and true afterwards, with checkBundle returning VERIFIED over what then read as an UNBOUNDED scope. THIS IS THE MUTABLE-INPUT RULE THE WORLD/AUTHORITY LADDER ALREADY REACHED, rediscovered independently by the proof subsystem: do not authenticate one read of caller-owned data and continue reasoning from later reads of it. P4.1 already snapshotted everything it fetched from an untrusted store and then stopped touching the store; the ROOT input had no equivalent transition, so the one artifact a verifier is handed directly was the one artifact it did not own. THE PREFERRED PUBLIC BOUNDARY IS BYTES -- check*Bytes(rawBytes) -> strict canonical ingress -> owned plain data -> checker -- because bytes cannot have a getter. An object convenience API is legitimate provided it canonicalises ONCE and then uses only the owned snapshot; the one read taken at ingress is the read the verdict is about.
